goals-picker-subtitle: Pick something you want to work on. You set it, you finish it.
goals-none: You haven't set any goals yet.
goals-resolve-note: Finishing a goal earns {{xp}} Resolve XP.
goals-ask-ai-failed: Couldn't get suggestions just now. Pick one yourself.
goals-method-ai-desc: I look at what you have practised and what you tend to avoid, then suggest goals that fit.
goals-method-own-desc: Pick an area yourself and decide how much to take on.
goals-where-method: Every exercise type can count, but you get to act at a different moment in each one.
goals-where-exercise-type: Every exercise type counts. This goal only says which ones you pick.
goals-where-self-explanation: Only Efficiency and Matching have an explain-your-reasoning step. Suitability exercises will not move this goal.
goals-where-method-comparison: Only Suitability exercises compare two methods. No other type will move this goal.
goals-in-method-suitability: You get all three methods to choose from and solve with the one you want. There is no wrong answer here.
goals-in-method-efficiency: You get the same three choices, but only the method that fits this system is accepted. Pick one that does not fit and the exercise tells you it is not efficient and asks you to choose again.
goals-in-method-matching: You do not pick the method here. The exercise names it, and asks which of several systems needs no reshaping instead.
goals-in-exercise-type: Nothing to decide inside the exercise. Every exercise you finish of the type you picked counts.
goals-in-self-explanation-efficiency: Once you pick the method that fits, it asks whether you want to explain why that method suits the system. Say yes and write your reason.
goals-in-self-explanation-matching: Once you pick the right system, it asks whether you want to explain why that system is the right one. Say yes and write your reason.
goals-in-method-comparison: Solve with a suitable method and it shows you how a classmate solved the same system, then asks whether you want to compare the two approaches. Say yes.
goals-in-solve-on-own: When it asks whether you want to find the solution to an equation on your own, say yes instead of asking to be shown it.
goals-in-hints-and-errors: This counts the hints you open and the wrong answers you give. Your limit applies to each exercise on its own.
goals-focus-method-efficiency: Because you picked {{method}}, this only counts when {{method}} is the method that fits.
goals-focus-method-matching: Because you picked {{method}}, this only counts when the exercise happens to use {{method}}.
goals-suggestions-unavailable: This suggestion doesn't match the goal menu. Pick one yourself.
goals-cat-method-desc: Practise one method: elimination, substitution or equalization.
goals-cat-exercise-type-desc: Focus on one kind of exercise: suitability, efficiency or matching.
goals-cat-self-explanation-desc: Put your thinking into words instead of jumping straight to the answer.
goals-cat-method-comparison-desc: Weigh two methods against each other before you choose.
goals-cat-solve-on-own-desc: Reach the solution on your own before reaching for help.
goals-cat-hints-errors-desc: Complete exercises while staying under a limit you choose.
milestone-subtitle: You've crossed the {{milestone}} XP milestone. Keep it up. Next stop: {{next}} XP!
nudge-ask: Would you like to give it a try?
nudge-evidence: I've offered this {{opportunities}} times, and you've taken it up {{engaged}} of them.
nudge-element-self-explanation: Explaining your reasoning in your own words
nudge-element-method-comparison: Comparing two methods before you pick one
nudge-benefit-self-explanation: Putting your thinking into words is what makes a method stick. Students who explain their reasoning remember it far longer than students who just watch it done.
nudge-benefit-method-comparison: Comparing methods is how you learn which one actually fits the system, instead of always reaching for the same one.
nudge-benefit-solve-on-own: Trying it yourself first, even when you get it wrong, is what builds the skill. Watching the answer does not.
nudge-footnote: I'll only bring this up again if the pattern keeps growing.
dashboard-improve-area-hint: Try more {{type}} exercises to grow in this area.

tree-need-branches: Grow your Branches (Insight XP) to hang your fruits.

tour-offer-companions-title: Want a quick look at your buddy?
tour-offer-companions-body: Two minutes on the buddy corner: how to change who you study with, and what the XP you earn unlocks. You can also just carry on. The tour stays available here afterwards.
tour-offer-exercises-title: Want a quick look at the exercises?
tour-offer-exercises-body: Two minutes on the exercises: the three kinds, what each one asks of you, and inside a real one so you know what to expect. You can also just carry on. The tour stays available here afterwards.
tour-buddy-body: If you're stuck, ask me for a hint. When you finish, earn points for telling me how it went. More buddies unlock when you level up!
tour-skills-body: You get points for the choices you make, not for correct answers. You can be wrong and still get points! Curious how it works?
tour-xp-body: Each skill has its own points, and each one is counted separately.
tour-xp-note: You can't lose points. Leveling up unlocks new buddies and outfits!
tour-tree-body:
It shows how your three skills build on each other:
- Roots = Choice XP
- Branches = Insight XP
- Fruits = Resolve XP
A full tree needs all three: fruit hangs from branches, branches grow from roots.
tour-tree-note: This is your tree right now. On your first day it is mostly bare ground, and that is exactly how it should look before you have earned anything.
tour-dashboard-intro-body: It gives you an overview of where you stand. Let me walk you through it.
tour-progress-body: Here you see how many points you earned in each skill.
tour-progress-note: Tap the info button to see how to earn them.
tour-tabs-body:
From here you can:
- try an exercise, then check the Analytics board and your Growth Tree
- see how others are doing on the Leaderboard
tour-buddy-corner-body: {{name}} sits in the corner of every screen while you work. Tap your companion to choose a different one, or to open the wardrobe.
tour-characters-title: New companions unlock with your points
tour-characters-body: Pippin is yours from the first day. The other three unlock at level 3 of one wallet each: Chimi at Choice level 3, Master Zen at Insight level 3, and Lumi at Resolve level 3. This is the real screen, shown as a demo, so nothing here gets saved.
tour-characters-note: Level 3 means 150 points in that wallet. The three wallets fill up separately, so each companion is reached by earning in a different way.
tour-outfits-body: Each companion's outfits unlock with the same wallet that unlocked them. You start with one look, and every level above it opens another one. Once an outfit is yours, wearing it costs nothing.
tour-outfits-note: Level 1 starts at 50 points, level 3 at 150 and level 5 at 400.
tour-goals-body:
Set a goal, like doing 5 exercises, and I'll keep track of when you achieve it.
Two ways to choose one:
- Choosing a goal I suggest
- Setting a goal for yourself (earns you Choice XP, because deciding is a skill)
tour-picker-categories-body: Every one of these is something I already keep track of, so any goal you set can be checked. Compare two methods, explain your reasoning, solve it without hints. Whichever you choose, I can tell whether you did it.
tour-picker-target-body: Choose how you want to be measured, and how many times. Some goals also let you pick which exercise types should count. The defaults are already filled in, so you can just press Add if you like.
tour-picker-where-title: Where you can work on it
tour-picker-where-body: These are the exercise types that can move your goal, and under each one it says what you actually have to do inside it. Comparing two methods, for example, only turns up in a Suitability exercise.
tour-picker-add-body: This saves the goal and starts counting. From this moment on, every exercise you finish moves it forward.
tour-goal-set-body: Your goal now sits on the dashboard with a progress bar, starting at zero. It shows you what is left, and every exercise you finish moves it along. When you complete it you earn Resolve XP.
tour-to-training-body: A goal is only a target. The real work happens in the flexibility exercises, and they are right here on your dashboard. Let me show you what they look like.
tour-flex-list-body: Every exercise you can do, in order. The ones you have finished are marked, and you can repeat any of them. Repeating is often how a goal gets met.
tour-flex-info-body: Knowing how to use a method is one skill. Knowing which method suits a particular system is a different one, and it is the hard one to practise from a textbook. That second skill is what these exercises are for.
tour-flex-types-body: The list mixes three kinds together. All of them ask you to solve a system, but they ask you different questions. Here is what each one is really testing.
tour-visual-suitability-what: You get a system and choose the method that suits it.
tour-visual-efficiency-what: You get a system and choose the method that needs the least rearranging first.
tour-visual-matching-what: This one works the other way round. You are given a method and choose the system that suits it.
tour-ex-task-body: Every exercise starts by telling you what you are looking at. This is a real exercise, the same screen you get when you press one, but nothing you do here is counted.
tour-ex-system-body: This is the system of equations you are working with. Every exercise gives you one and asks you to think about which method suits it.
tour-ex-choose-body: This is where the exercise stops being a task and becomes a choice. Which method suits this system? Deciding on purpose, then finding out whether you were right, is the skill we are building.
tour-ex-help-body: Ask for a hint whenever you want. It shows you the next step, never the answer. Asking costs you nothing, but a run with no hints is one of the goals you can set, so either way it gets counted.
tour-done-body: Pick something you want to get better at, then go and do the exercises that count towards it. Your dashboard keeps track of the rest. You can replay this walkthrough anytime with the question mark button at the top of your dashboard.
